Description: THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE THE PERSONNEL, MATERIALS, EQUIPMENT, AND FACILITIES NECESSARY FOR DESIGN, ANALYSIS, DEVELOPMENT, FABRICATION, ASSEMBLY, TESTING, CALIBRATION, QUALIFICATION, ACCEPTANCE, STORAGE, STORAGE TESTING, AND SUPPORT FOR SPACECRAFT INTEGRATION AND LAUNCH OF ADVANCED MICROWAVE SOUNDING UNIT-A (AMSU-A) PROTO-FLIGHT MODEL (PFM).  VARIOUS ANALYTICAL MODELS AND TEST MODELS ARE REQUIRED. THE EFFORT INCLUDES GROUND SUPPORT EQUIPMENT AND TEST AND CALIBRATION EQUIPMENT.  IT ALSO INCLUDES A DESIGN CONCEPT REVIEW INSTRUMENT DELIVERY, STORAGE, POST-DELIVERY BENCH TESTING, SPACECRAFT INTEGRATION SUPPORT, PRE-LAUNCH AND POST-LAUNCH SUPPORT.  REPORTING, REVIEWS AND DOCUMENTATION OF ALL ASPECTS OF THE PROGRAM ARE REQUIRED. THE DELIVERABLE EARTH OBSERVING SYSTEM (EOS) AMSU-A INSTRUMENT IS A PFM AND OPTIONAL FLIGHT MODEL (FM).AMSU-A IS PLANNED FOR FLIGHT ON THE EOS PM SPACECRAFT.  AMSU-A SHALL BE COMPATIBLE WITH THE EOS PM SPACECRAFT INTERFACES, AND   SHALL MEET THE IN-ORBIT LIFETIME REQUIREMENT OF 3 YEARS WITH A GOAL OF 5 YEARS WITHOUT IN-ORBIT SERVICING.THE PROGRAM PHASE LEADING TO DELIVERY OF THE PFM SHALL BE REFERRED TO AS THE "BASIC PHASE" AND SHALL BE SUBDIVIDED INTO TWO SUB-PHASES, THE "SUPPORT PHASE" AND THE "IMPLEMENTATION PHASE." THE SUPPORT PHASE SHALL PROVIDE TECHNICAL AND PROGRAM MANAGEMENT SUPPORT TO ADDRESS: (1) THE EVOLVING SPACECRAFT INTERFACES, (2) SPECIAL INSTRUMENT STUDIES AND (3) PROGRAM PLANNING FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION PHASE.  THE IMPLEMENTATION PHASE SHALL INCLUDE THE DESIGN, FABRICATION, ASSEMBLY, TESTING AND DELIVERY OF THE PFM AND SHALL START WITH A PROGRAM INITIATION MEETING.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ALSO PROVIDE THE PERSONNEL, MATERIALS, EQUIPMENT,  AND FACILITIES NECESSARY FOR REDESIGN (IF NECESSARY), ANALYSIS, DEVELOPMENT, FABRICATION, ASSEMBLY, TESTING, CALIBRATION, QUALIFICATION, ACCEPTANCE, AND SUPPORT FOR SPACECRAFT INTEGRATION AND LAUNCH OF METEOROLOGICAL SATELLITES (METSAT) AMSU-A FM INSTRUMENTS.DEVELOPMENT OF THE METSAT AMSU-A INSTRUMENT WILL BE CONDUCTED IN FOUR TECHNICAL PHASES. PHASE 1 SHALL BE AN ASSESSMENT TO DETERMINE WHAT AREAS OF THE METSAT INSTRUMENT REQUIRE REDESIGN. OBSOLETE COMPONENTS ARE TO BE REPLACED BY NEW COMPONENTS ONLY AFTER DESIGN ANALYSIS HAS BEEN PERFORMED AND MARGINS ARE ANALYTICALLY DEMONSTRATED. IMPROVEMENTS THAT HAVE HERITAGE IN THE EOS AMSU-A INSTRUMENT SHALL BE CONSIDERED AND PRESENTED TO THE GOVERNMENT FOR APPROVAL. PHASE 2 SHALL MAKE AN ASSESSMENT OF ALL DRAWINGS, PROCUREMENTS SPECIFICATIONS, MANUFACTURING FLOWS, SHOP ORDERS, TEST FIXTURES, TEST EQUIPMENT AND TEST PROCEDURES IN ORDER TO IDENTIFY AREAS THAT ARE DEFICIENT AND/OR REQUIRE UPGRADES.  PHASE 3 WILL ACCOMPLISH THOSE ITEMS IDENTIFIED AS A RESULT OF PHASES 1 AND 2.  PHASE 4 IS THE IMPLEMENTATION PHASE WHICH INCLUDES THE FABRICATION, TEST AND CALIBRATION OF THE METSAT INSTRUMENTS.

THE MAIN PURPOSE OF THIS PROGRAM IS TO PRODUCE AND DELIVER TO NASA THREE TRACKING AND DATA RELAY SATELLITES DESIGNATED AS TDRS H, I AND J. THESE SATELLITES WILL BE USED TO CONTINUE THE PRESENT FUNCTION OF THE EXISTING TDRS SPACECRAFT. THE TDRS H, I AND J SHALL BE FULLY COMPATIBLE WITH, AND BE CAPABLE OF FUNCTIONING AS A PART OF, THE TRACKING AND DATA RELAY SATELLITE SYSTEM (TDRSS) AS IMPLEMENTED AND OPERATED BY THE WHITE SANDS COMPLEX (WSC) WHICH INCLUDES THE SECOND TDRS GROUND TERMINAL (STGT) AND THE WHITE SANDS GROUND TERMINAL UPGRADE (WSGTU). THE TDRS H, I, AND J PROGRAM SHALL ENCOMPASS ALL OF THE EFFORTS REQUIRED TO DESIGN, DEVELOP, BUILD, TEST, SHIP, AND SUPPORT THE LAUNCH AND ON-ORBIT ACTIVATION OF THREE TRACKING AND DATA RELAY SATELLITES. THESE SATELLITES SHALL BE DELIVERED TO NASA AT THE EASTERN TEST RANGE. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR PROVIDING NECESSARY EFFORTS REQUIRED FOR THE PRE-LAUNCH AND LAUNCH OPERATIONS WITH THE EXPENDABLE LAUNCHVEHICLE PROVIDED BY THE GOVERNMENT. UPON SUCCESSFUL INJECTION INTO A GEOSYNCHRONOUS ORBIT, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM A CHECKOUT AND ACTIVATION OF THE SPACECRAFT AND SHALL SUPPORT THE INTEGRATION OF THE SPACECRAFT INTO THE OPERATIONAL SPACE NETWORK. THE CONTRACTOR IS REQUIRED TO DELIVER THREE SATELLITES THAT ARE FULLY COMPATIBLE AND OPERATIONAL WITH THE REMAINDER OF THE TDRSS AND ALL TDRSS USERS. CHANGES TO THE EXISTING SPACE-TO-SPACE LINK BETWEEN THE TDRS AND THE USERS, AND CHANGES TO OTHER EXISTING OPERATIONAL INTERFACES BETWEEN USER SPACECRAFT AND EXISTING USER SERVICES ARE NOT PERMITTED. THE WSC, IN ITS STGT AND WSGTU IMPLEMENTATION, WILL OPERATE THE TDRS H, I AND J TO PROVIDE THE SPECIFIED USER SERVICES. THE CONTRACTOR'S DELIVERED SATELLITES AND OTHER EFFORTS MUST MEET ALL SPECIFICATIONS OF TDRS-RP-SY-001. THE OPERATIONS OF THE TDRS H, I, AND J SYSTEM AND SPACECRAFT SHALL, QUANTITATIVELY ANDQUALITATIVELY, PERFORM AS WELL AS OR BETTER THAN THE EXISTING TDRS AND THE EXISTING WSC FLIGHT OPERATIONS. THE KA-BAND OPTION SERVICE SHALL HAVE ALL OF THE ATTRIBUTES OF THE EXISTING KU-BAND SERVICE EXCEPT FOR THE FULL TIME SIMULATION AND VERIFICATION CAPABILITY KNOWN IN THE STGT IMPLEMENTATION AS THE END-TO-END TEST SYSTEM. THE CHANGES MADE BY THE CONTRACTOR TO THE WSC MUST NOT ADVERSELY AFFECT THE OPERATIONS OF THE WSC WITH THE F-L THROUGH F-7 SPACECRAFT. ADDITIONALLY, THE EFFORT OF IMPLEMENTING THESE CHANGES BY THE CONTRACTOR SHALL NOT CAUSE ANY ADVERSE IMPACTS TO ON-GOING OPERATIONS EXCEPT FOR THE TEMPORARY REMOVAL OF A SINGLE SGLT AT A TIME. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ALSO DESIGN, DEVELOP, IMPLEMENT, TEST AND DELIVER THE TDRS H, I, AND J SPACECRAFT EMULATOR (TSE) AND THE REAL-TIME TELEMETRY MONITORING SYSTEM (RTMS).

Description: PHASE 1 DEVELOPMENT OF TECHNOLOGY ELEMENTS OF THE NASA'S EVOLUTIONARY XENON THRUSTER (NEXT), INCLUDING POWER PROCESSING UNIT AND SYSTEM  ENGINEERING AND INTEGRATION. CONTRACTOR IS BOEING ELECTRON DYNAMIC DEVICES._CONTRACT NAS3-02158. TECHNOLOGY EFFORTS IN THIS PROGRAM ARE INTENDED TO ENABLE THE DESIGN OF HIGH-PERFORMANCE, HIGH-POWER, ION PROPULSION SYSTEMS. Description: THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE THE PERSONNEL, MATERIALS, EQUIPMENT, AND FACILITIES NECESSARY FOR DESIGN, ANALYSIS, DEVELOPMENT, FABRICATION, ASSEMBLY, TESTING, CALIBRATION, QUALIFICATION, ACCEPTANCE, STORAGE, STORAGE TESTING, AND SUPPORT FOR SPACECRAFT INTEGRATION AND LAUNCH OF ADVANCED MICROWAVE SOUNDING UNIT-A (AMSU-A) PROTO-FLIGHT MODEL (PFM).  VARIOUS ANALYTICAL MODELS AND TEST MODELS ARE REQUIRED. THE EFFORT INCLUDES GROUND SUPPORT EQUIPMENT AND TEST AND CALIBRATION EQUIPMENT.  IT ALSO INCLUDES A DESIGN CONCEPT REVIEW INSTRUMENT DELIVERY, STORAGE, POST-DELIVERY BENCH TESTING, SPACECRAFT INTEGRATION SUPPORT, PRE-LAUNCH AND POST-LAUNCH SUPPORT.  REPORTING, REVIEWS AND DOCUMENTATION OF ALL ASPECTS OF THE PROGRAM ARE REQUIRED. THE DELIVERABLE EARTH OBSERVING SYSTEM (EOS) AMSU-A INSTRUMENT IS A PFM AND OPTIONAL FLIGHT MODEL (FM).AMSU-A IS PLANNED FOR FLIGHT ON THE EOS PM SPACECRAFT.  AMSU-A SHALL BE COMPATIBLE WITH THE EOS PM SPACECRAFT INTERFACES, AND   SHALL MEET THE IN-ORBIT LIFETIME REQUIREMENT OF 3 YEARS WITH A GOAL OF 5 YEARS WITHOUT IN-ORBIT SERVICING.THE PROGRAM PHASE LEADING TO DELIVERY OF THE PFM SHALL BE REFERRED TO AS THE "BASIC PHASE" AND SHALL BE SUBDIVIDED INTO TWO SUB-PHASES, THE "SUPPORT PHASE" AND THE "IMPLEMENTATION PHASE." THE SUPPORT PHASE SHALL PROVIDE TECHNICAL AND PROGRAM MANAGEMENT SUPPORT TO ADDRESS: (1) THE EVOLVING SPACECRAFT INTERFACES, (2) SPECIAL INSTRUMENT STUDIES AND (3) PROGRAM PLANNING FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION PHASE.  THE IMPLEMENTATION PHASE SHALL INCLUDE THE DESIGN, FABRICATION, ASSEMBLY, TESTING AND DELIVERY OF THE PFM AND SHALL START WITH A PROGRAM INITIATION MEETING.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ALSO PROVIDE THE PERSONNEL, MATERIALS, EQUIPMENT,  AND FACILITIES NECESSARY FOR REDESIGN (IF NECESSARY), ANALYSIS, DEVELOPMENT, FABRICATION, ASSEMBLY, TESTING, CALIBRATION, QUALIFICATION, ACCEPTANCE, AND SUPPORT FOR SPACECRAFT INTEGRATION AND LAUNCH OF METEOROLOGICAL SATELLITES (METSAT) AMSU-A FM INSTRUMENTS.DEVELOPMENT OF THE METSAT AMSU-A INSTRUMENT WILL BE CONDUCTED IN FOUR TECHNICAL PHASES. PHASE 1 SHALL BE AN ASSESSMENT TO DETERMINE WHAT AREAS OF THE METSAT INSTRUMENT REQUIRE REDESIGN. OBSOLETE COMPONENTS ARE TO BE REPLACED BY NEW COMPONENTS ONLY AFTER DESIGN ANALYSIS HAS BEEN PERFORMED AND MARGINS ARE ANALYTICALLY DEMONSTRATED. IMPROVEMENTS THAT HAVE HERITAGE IN THE EOS AMSU-A INSTRUMENT SHALL BE CONSIDERED AND PRESENTED TO THE GOVERNMENT FOR APPROVAL. PHASE 2 SHALL MAKE AN ASSESSMENT OF ALL DRAWINGS, PROCUREMENTS SPECIFICATIONS, MANUFACTURING FLOWS, SHOP ORDERS, TEST FIXTURES, TEST EQUIPMENT AND TEST PROCEDURES IN ORDER TO IDENTIFY AREAS THAT ARE DEFICIENT AND/OR REQUIRE UPGRADES.  PHASE 3 WILL ACCOMPLISH THOSE ITEMS IDENTIFIED AS A RESULT OF PHASES 1 AND 2.  PHASE 4 IS THE IMPLEMENTATION PHASE WHICH INCLUDES THE FABRICATION, TEST AND CALIBRATION OF THE METSAT INSTRUMENTS.

PHASE 1 SHALL BE AN ASSESSMENT TO DETERMINE WHAT AREAS OF THE METSAT INSTRUMENT REQUIRE REDESIGN. OBSOLETE COMPONENTS ARE TO BE REPLACED BY NEW COMPONENTS ONLY AFTER DESIGN ANALYSIS HAS BEEN PERFORMED AND MARGINS ARE ANALYTICALLY DEMONSTRATED. IMPROVEMENTS THAT HAVE HERITAGE IN THE EOS AMSU-A INSTRUMENT SHALL BE CONSIDERED AND PRESENTED TO THE GOVERNMENT FOR APPROVAL. PHASE 2 SHALL MAKE AN ASSESSMENT OF ALL DRAWINGS, PROCUREMENTS SPECIFICATIONS, MANUFACTURING FLOWS, SHOP ORDERS, TEST FIXTURES, TEST EQUIPMENT AND TEST PROCEDURES IN ORDER TO IDENTIFY AREAS THAT ARE DEFICIENT AND/OR REQUIRE UPGRADES.  PHASE 3 WILL ACCOMPLISH THOSE ITEMS IDENTIFIED AS A RESULT OF PHASES 1 AND 2.  PHASE 4 IS THE IMPLEMENTATION PHASE WHICH INCLUDES THE FABRICATION, TEST AND CALIBRATION OF THE METSAT INSTRUMENTS.

AMSU-A SHALL BE COMPATIBLE WITH THE EOS PM SPACECRAFT INTERFACES, AND   SHALL MEET THE IN-ORBIT LIFETIME REQUIREMENT OF 3 YEARS WITH A GOAL OF 5 YEARS WITHOUT IN-ORBIT SERVICING.THE PROGRAM PHASE LEADING TO DELIVERY OF THE PFM SHALL BE REFERRED TO AS THE "BASIC PHASE" AND SHALL BE SUBDIVIDED INTO TWO SUB-PHASES, THE "SUPPORT PHASE" AND THE "IMPLEMENTATION PHASE." THE SUPPORT PHASE SHALL PROVIDE TECHNICAL AND PROGRAM MANAGEMENT SUPPORT TO ADDRESS: (1) THE EVOLVING SPACECRAFT INTERFACES, (2) SPECIAL INSTRUMENT STUDIES AND (3) PROGRAM PLANNING FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION PHASE. PHASE 1 SHALL BE AN ASSESSMENT TO DETERMINE WHAT AREAS OF THE METSAT INSTRUMENT REQUIRE REDESIGN. OBSOLETE COMPONENTS ARE TO BE REPLACED BY NEW COMPONENTS ONLY AFTER DESIGN ANALYSIS HAS BEEN PERFORMED AND MARGINS ARE ANALYTICALLY DEMONSTRATED. IMPROVEMENTS THAT HAVE HERITAGE IN THE EOS AMSU-A INSTRUMENT SHALL BE CONSIDERED AND PRESENTED TO THE GOVERNMENT FOR APPROVAL. PHASE 2 SHALL MAKE AN ASSESSMENT OF ALL DRAWINGS, PROCUREMENTS SPECIFICATIONS, MANUFACTURING FLOWS, SHOP ORDERS, TEST FIXTURES, TEST EQUIPMENT AND TEST PROCEDURES IN ORDER TO IDENTIFY AREAS THAT ARE DEFICIENT AND/OR REQUIRE UPGRADES.  PHASE 3 WILL ACCOMPLISH THOSE ITEMS IDENTIFIED AS A RESULT OF PHASES 1 AND 2.  PHASE 4 IS THE IMPLEMENTATION PHASE WHICH INCLUDES THE FABRICATION, TEST AND CALIBRATION OF THE METSAT INSTRUMENTS.

VARIOUS ANALYTICAL MODELS AND TEST MODELS ARE REQUIRED. THE EFFORT INCLUDES GROUND SUPPORT EQUIPMENT AND TEST AND CALIBRATION EQUIPMENT.  IT ALSO INCLUDES A DESIGN CONCEPT REVIEW INSTRUMENT DELIVERY, STORAGE, POST-DELIVERY BENCH TESTING, SPACECRAFT INTEGRATION SUPPORT, PRE-LAUNCH AND POST-LAUNCH SUPPORT.  REPORTING, REVIEWS AND DOCUMENTATION OF ALL ASPECTS OF THE PROGRAM ARE REQUIRED. THE DELIVERABLE EARTH OBSERVING SYSTEM (EOS) AMSU-A INSTRUMENT IS A PFM AND OPTIONAL FLIGHT MODEL (FM).AMSU-A IS PLANNED FOR FLIGHT ON THE EOS PM SPACECRAFT.  AMSU-A SHALL BE COMPATIBLE WITH THE EOS PM SPACECRAFT INTERFACES, AND   SHALL MEET THE IN-ORBIT LIFETIME REQUIREMENT OF 3 YEARS WITH A GOAL OF 5 YEARS WITHOUT IN-ORBIT SERVICING.THE PROGRAM PHASE LEADING TO DELIVERY OF THE PFM SHALL BE REFERRED TO AS THE "BASIC PHASE" AND SHALL BE SUBDIVIDED INTO TWO SUB-PHASES, THE "SUPPORT PHASE" AND THE "IMPLEMENTATION PHASE." THE SUPPORT PHASE SHALL PROVIDE TECHNICAL AND PROGRAM MANAGEMENT SUPPORT TO ADDRESS: (1) THE EVOLVING SPACECRAFT INTERFACES, (2) SPECIAL INSTRUMENT STUDIES AND (3) PROGRAM PLANNING FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION PHASE.  THE IMPLEMENTATION PHASE SHALL INCLUDE THE DESIGN, FABRICATION, ASSEMBLY, TESTING AND DELIVERY OF THE PFM AND SHALL START WITH A PROGRAM INITIATION MEETING.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ALSO PROVIDE THE PERSONNEL, MATERIALS, EQUIPMENT,  AND FACILITIES NECESSARY FOR REDESIGN (IF NECESSARY), ANALYSIS, DEVELOPMENT, FABRICATION, ASSEMBLY, TESTING, CALIBRATION, QUALIFICATION, ACCEPTANCE, AND SUPPORT FOR SPACECRAFT INTEGRATION AND LAUNCH OF METEOROLOGICAL SATELLITES (METSAT) AMSU-A FM INSTRUMENTS.DEVELOPMENT OF THE METSAT AMSU-A INSTRUMENT WILL BE CONDUCTED IN FOUR TECHNICAL PHASES. PHASE 1 SHALL BE AN ASSESSMENT TO DETERMINE WHAT AREAS OF THE METSAT INSTRUMENT REQUIRE REDESIGN. OBSOLETE COMPONENTS ARE TO BE REPLACED BY NEW COMPONENTS ONLY AFTER DESIGN ANALYSIS HAS BEEN PERFORMED AND MARGINS ARE ANALYTICALLY DEMONSTRATED. IMPROVEMENTS THAT HAVE HERITAGE IN THE EOS AMSU-A INSTRUMENT SHALL BE CONSIDERED AND PRESENTED TO THE GOVERNMENT FOR APPROVAL. PHASE 2 SHALL MAKE AN ASSESSMENT OF ALL DRAWINGS, PROCUREMENTS SPECIFICATIONS, MANUFACTURING FLOWS, SHOP ORDERS, TEST FIXTURES, TEST EQUIPMENT AND TEST PROCEDURES IN ORDER TO IDENTIFY AREAS THAT ARE DEFICIENT AND/OR REQUIRE UPGRADES.  PHASE 3 WILL ACCOMPLISH THOSE ITEMS IDENTIFIED AS A RESULT OF PHASES 1 AND 2.  PHASE 4 IS THE IMPLEMENTATION PHASE WHICH INCLUDES THE FABRICATION, TEST AND CALIBRATION OF THE METSAT INSTRUMENTS.

Description: CENTER FOR CELL MIMETIC SPACE EXPLORATION CMISE - IN BOTH LIVING SYSTEMS AND IN SPACECRAFT, REAMS OF INFORMATION FROM MULTIPLE SCALES NEED TO BE ACQUIRED AND ACTED ON AT MULTIPLE SCALES.  IN FACT, THE SUPERMOLECULE, THE BIOLOGICAL CELL, THE ASTRONAUTS BODY AND THE SPACESHIP, THOUGH VARYING WIDELY IN SIZES, ARE ALL COMPLEX SYSTEMS PERFORMING COHERENT FUNCTIONS THROUGH HIGHLY DISTRIBUTED MECHANISMS OF SENSING.  INFORMATION PROCESSING AND ACTUATION.  TRANSCENDING ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE DIFFERENCES IN LENGTH SCALES, UCLA VIEWS THE SUPERMOLECULE, THE BIOLOGICAL CELL, THE ASTRONAUTS BODY AND THE SPACE VEHICLE AS CELLS, OBSERVATION POINTS WHERE COHERENCE OF INFORMATION EMERGES FROM COMPLEXITY.  THESE CELLS ARE SYSTEMS THAT MIMIC THE MODES OF INFORMATION PROCESSING NORMALLY ATTRIBUTED TO BIOLOGICAL CELLS.  THE APPLICATION OF NATURES STRATEGY OF DISTRIBUTED MULTILEVEL INFORMATION COLLECTION AND MANAGEMENT IS THE THREAD THAT WILL ACHIEVE A SEAMLESS LINK BETWEEN THE MOLECULAR SCALE NANOTECHNOLOGY OF SENSORS, ACTUATORS AND COMPUTATION, THE ASTRONAUTS AND THE SPACE VEHICLE.  BY MIMICKING THE COMPLEXITY OF MULTISCALE INFORMATION MANAGEMENT OF LIVING SYSTEMS COUPLED WITH THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW NANO TECHNOLOGIES, SPACE EXPLORATION WILL ENTER A NEW ERA.  WITH THIS OUT-OF-BOX CONCEPT, UCLA PROPOSED THE INSTITUTE FOR CELL MIMETIC SPACE EXPLORATION (CMISE).  THIS INSTITUTE WILL BE DEVOTED TO THE - DEVELOPMENT OF CELL MIMETIC SYSTEMS, CONSISTING OF SENSORS, ACTUATORS AND ENERGY SOURCES.  DEVELOPMENT OF MULTI-SCALE INFORMATION PROCESSING TECHNIQUES, I.E., INFORMATICS.  DEVELOPMENT OF SCALABLE TECHNOLOGIES FOR SPACE BIOLOGICAL EXPERIMENTS, ASTRONAUT HEALTH MONITORING AND SPACESHIP RESOURCE MANAGEMENT.  DEVELOPMENT OF AN INTERDISCIPLINARY EDUCATION PROGRAM FOR EDUCATING FUTURE GENERATIONS OF YOUNG SPACE ENGINEERS AND SCIENTISTS.  CMISE ENVISIONS THAT ITS STRATEGY OF USING THE BIOLOGICAL MODEL OF HIERARCHICAL CELLULAR ORGANIZATION FOR THE APPLICATION OF NANOTECHNOLOGY AND THE MANAGEMENT OF INFORMATION WILL BE THE MODEL OF SPACE SYSTEM DESIGN THAT WILL DEFINE THE TECHNOLOGY FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS OF SPACE EXPLORERS.  THE GOAL OF THE CMISE EDUCATION PROGRAM IS TO TRAIN A CONTINUOUS STREAM OF YOUNG SPACE EXPLORERS.  THE PROGRAM WILL ENCOMPASS THE ENTIRE EDUCATIONAL SPECTRUM:  THE DEVELOPMENT OF LEARNING TOOLS FOR K-12, RESEARCH EXPERIENCES FOR UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS AND SUPPORT FOR PH.D. GRADUATE TRAINING.  SPECIAL ATTENTION WILL BE PAID TO THE RECRUITMENT OF UNDER-REPRESENTED STUDENTS.  STUDENTS OF THE CMISE PROGRAM WILL BE TRAINED IN A NEW GENERATION OF CROSS-DISCIPLINARY TECHNOLOGIES THAT ARE ABSOLUTELY NECESSARY TO SUPPORT THE NEXT GENERATION OF SPACE EXPLORERS.

THE MAIN PURPOSE OF THIS PROGRAM IS TO PRODUCE AND DELIVER TO NASA THREE TRACKING AND DATA RELAY SATELLITES DESIGNATED AS TDRS H, I AND J. THESE SATELLITES WILL BE USED TO CONTINUE THE PRESENT FUNCTION OF THE EXISTING TDRS SPACECRAFT. THE TDRS H, I AND J SHALL BE FULLY COMPATIBLE WITH, AND BE CAPABLE OF FUNCTIONING AS A PART OF, THE TRACKING AND DATA RELAY SATELLITE SYSTEM (TDRSS) AS IMPLEMENTED AND OPERATED BY THE WHITE SANDS COMPLEX (WSC) WHICH INCLUDES THE SECOND TDRS GROUND TERMINAL (STGT) AND THE WHITE SANDS GROUND TERMINAL UPGRADE (WSGTU). THE TDRS H, I, AND J PROGRAM SHALL ENCOMPASS ALL OF THE EFFORTS REQUIRED TO DESIGN, DEVELOP, BUILD, TEST, SHIP, AND SUPPORT THE LAUNCH AND ON-ORBIT ACTIVATION OF THREE TRACKING AND DATA RELAY SATELLITES. THESE SATELLITES SHALL BE DELIVERED TO NASA AT THE EASTERN TEST RANGE. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR PROVIDING NECESSARY EFFORTS REQUIRED FOR THE PRE-LAUNCH AND LAUNCH OPERATIONS WITH THE EXPENDABLE LAUNCHVEHICLE PROVIDED BY THE GOVERNMENT. UPON SUCCESSFUL INJECTION INTO A GEOSYNCHRONOUS ORBIT, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM A CHECKOUT AND ACTIVATION OF THE SPACECRAFT AND SHALL SUPPORT THE INTEGRATION OF THE SPACECRAFT INTO THE OPERATIONAL SPACE NETWORK. THE CONTRACTOR IS REQUIRED TO DELIVER THREE SATELLITES THAT ARE FULLY COMPATIBLE AND OPERATIONAL WITH THE REMAINDER OF THE TDRSS AND ALL TDRSS USERS. CHANGES TO THE EXISTING SPACE-TO-SPACE LINK BETWEEN THE TDRS AND THE USERS, AND CHANGES TO OTHER EXISTING OPERATIONAL INTERFACES BETWEEN USER SPACECRAFT AND EXISTING USER SERVICES ARE NOT PERMITTED. THE WSC, IN ITS STGT AND WSGTU IMPLEMENTATION, WILL OPERATE THE TDRS H, I AND J TO PROVIDE THE SPECIFIED USER SERVICES. THE CONTRACTOR'S DELIVERED SATELLITES AND OTHER EFFORTS MUST MEET ALL SPECIFICATIONS OF TDRS-RP-SY-001. THE OPERATIONS OF THE TDRS H, I, AND J SYSTEM AND SPACECRAFT SHALL, QUANTITATIVELY ANDQUALITATIVELY, PERFORM AS WELL AS OR BETTER THAN THE EXISTING TDRS AND THE EXISTING WSC FLIGHT OPERATIONS. IN THE EVENT THAT THE CONTRACTOR'S SATELLITE DESIGN OR IMPLEMENTATION IS NOT FULLY COMPATIBLE AND OPERATIONAL WITH THE BASELINE WSC AND TDRSS AS PROVIDED BY NASA, THE CONTRACTOR IS RESPONSIBLE FOR DESIGNING, IMPLEMENTING, DOCUMENTING AND VALIDATING CHANGES TO THE WSC, TO ASSURE THE REQUIRED COMPATIBILITY AND OPERABILITY. THE KA-BAND OPTION SERVICE SHALL HAVE ALL OF THE ATTRIBUTES OF THE EXISTING KU-BAND SERVICE EXCEPT FOR THE FULL TIME SIMULATION AND VERIFICATION CAPABILITY KNOWN IN THE STGT IMPLEMENTATION AS THE END-TO-END TEST SYSTEM. THE BASELINE CONFIGURATION OF THE WSC INCLUDES SIX SPACE GROUND LINK TERMINALS (SGLT'S). FOUR SGLT'S SHALL BE CHANGED TO ACCOMMODATE THE TDRS H, I, AND J DESIGN. THE CHANGES MADE BY THE CONTRACTOR TO THE WSC MUST NOT ADVERSELY AFFECT THE OPERATIONS OF THE WSC WITH THE F-L THROUGH F-7 SPACECRAFT. ADDITIONALLY, THE EFFORT OF IMPLEMENTING THESE CHANGES BY THE CONTRACTOR SHALL NOT CAUSE ANY ADVERSE IMPACTS TO ON-GOING OPERATIONS EXCEPT FOR THE TEMPORARY REMOVAL OF A SINGLE SGLT AT A TIME. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ALSO DESIGN, DEVELOP, IMPLEMENT, TEST AND DELIVER THE TDRS H, I, AND J SPACECRAFT EMULATOR (TSE) AND THE REAL-TIME TELEMETRY MONITORING SYSTEM (RTMS).

SECTION 3, CHIEF ENGINEERS OFFICE SUPPORT: THIS SECTION DESCRIBES REQUIREMENTS FOR SUPPORT OF THE DFRC CHIEF ENGINEERS OFFICE AND INCLUDES SPECIAL PROJECTS AND STUDIES IN THE AREAS OF TOTAL RISK MANAGEMENT AND INDEPENDENT ASSESSMENT AND REVIEW. Description: THE PURPOSE OF THIS CONTRACT IS TO IMPLEMENT THE TRACKING AND DATA RELAY SATELLITE (TDRS) H, I, AND J PROGRAM. THE MAIN PURPOSE OF THIS PROGRAM IS TO PRODUCE AND DELIVER TO NASA THREE TRACKING AND DATA RELAY SATELLITES DESIGNATED AS TDRS H, I AND J. THESE SATELLITES WILL BE USED TO CONTINUE THE PRESENT FUNCTION OF THE EXISTING TDRS SPACECRAFT. THE TDRS H, I AND J SHALL BE FULLY COMPATIBLE WITH, AND BE CAPABLE OF FUNCTIONING AS A PART OF, THE TRACKING AND DATA RELAY SATELLITE SYSTEM (TDRSS) AS IMPLEMENTED AND OPERATED BY THE WHITE SANDS COMPLEX (WSC) WHICH INCLUDES THE SECOND TDRS GROUND TERMINAL (STGT) AND THE WHITE SANDS GROUND TERMINAL UPGRADE (WSGTU). THE TDRS H, I, AND J PROGRAM SHALL ENCOMPASS ALL OF THE EFFORTS REQUIRED TO DESIGN, DEVELOP, BUILD, TEST, SHIP, AND SUPPORT THE LAUNCH AND ON-ORBIT ACTIVATION OF THREE TRACKING AND DATA RELAY SATELLITES. THESE SATELLITES SHALL BE DELIVERED TO NASA AT THE EASTERN TEST RANGE. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR PROVIDING NECESSARY EFFORTS REQUIRED FOR THE PRE-LAUNCH AND LAUNCH OPERATIONS WITH THE EXPENDABLE LAUNCHVEHICLE PROVIDED BY THE GOVERNMENT. UPON SUCCESSFUL INJECTION INTO A GEOSYNCHRONOUS ORBIT, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM A CHECKOUT AND ACTIVATION OF THE SPACECRAFT AND SHALL SUPPORT THE INTEGRATION OF THE SPACECRAFT INTO THE OPERATIONAL SPACE NETWORK. THE CONTRACTOR IS REQUIRED TO DELIVER THREE SATELLITES THAT ARE FULLY COMPATIBLE AND OPERATIONAL WITH THE REMAINDER OF THE TDRSS AND ALL TDRSS USERS. CHANGES TO THE EXISTING SPACE-TO-SPACE LINK BETWEEN THE TDRS AND THE USERS, AND CHANGES TO OTHER EXISTING OPERATIONAL INTERFACES BETWEEN USER SPACECRAFT AND EXISTING USER SERVICES ARE NOT PERMITTED. THE WSC, IN ITS STGT AND WSGTU IMPLEMENTATION, WILL OPERATE THE TDRS H, I AND J TO PROVIDE THE SPECIFIED USER SERVICES. THE CONTRACTOR'S DELIVERED SATELLITES AND OTHER EFFORTS MUST MEET ALL SPECIFICATIONS OF TDRS-RP-SY-001. THE OPERATIONS OF THE TDRS H, I, AND J SYSTEM AND SPACECRAFT SHALL, QUANTITATIVELY ANDQUALITATIVELY, PERFORM AS WELL AS OR BETTER THAN THE EXISTING TDRS AND THE EXISTING WSC FLIGHT OPERATIONS. IN THE EVENT THAT THE CONTRACTOR'S SATELLITE DESIGN OR IMPLEMENTATION IS NOT FULLY COMPATIBLE AND OPERATIONAL WITH THE BASELINE WSC AND TDRSS AS PROVIDED BY NASA, THE CONTRACTOR IS RESPONSIBLE FOR DESIGNING, IMPLEMENTING, DOCUMENTING AND VALIDATING CHANGES TO THE WSC, TO ASSURE THE REQUIRED COMPATIBILITY AND OPERABILITY. THE KA-BAND OPTION SERVICE SHALL HAVE ALL OF THE ATTRIBUTES OF THE EXISTING KU-BAND SERVICE EXCEPT FOR THE FULL TIME SIMULATION AND VERIFICATION CAPABILITY KNOWN IN THE STGT IMPLEMENTATION AS THE END-TO-END TEST SYSTEM. THE BASELINE CONFIGURATION OF THE WSC INCLUDES SIX SPACE GROUND LINK TERMINALS (SGLT'S). FOUR SGLT'S SHALL BE CHANGED TO ACCOMMODATE THE TDRS H, I, AND J DESIGN. THE CHANGES MADE BY THE CONTRACTOR TO THE WSC MUST NOT ADVERSELY AFFECT THE OPERATIONS OF THE WSC WITH THE F-L THROUGH F-7 SPACECRAFT. ADDITIONALLY, THE EFFORT OF IMPLEMENTING THESE CHANGES BY THE CONTRACTOR SHALL NOT CAUSE ANY ADVERSE IMPACTS TO ON-GOING OPERATIONS EXCEPT FOR THE TEMPORARY REMOVAL OF A SINGLE SGLT AT A TIME. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ALSO DESIGN, DEVELOP, IMPLEMENT, TEST AND DELIVER THE TDRS H, I, AND J SPACECRAFT EMULATOR (TSE) AND THE REAL-TIME TELEMETRY MONITORING SYSTEM (RTMS).

OBSOLETE COMPONENTS ARE TO BE REPLACED BY NEW COMPONENTS ONLY AFTER DESIGN ANALYSIS HAS BEEN PERFORMED AND MARGINS ARE ANALYTICALLY DEMONSTRATED. Description: CENTER FOR CELL MIMETIC SPACE EXPLORATION CMISE - IN BOTH LIVING SYSTEMS AND IN SPACECRAFT, REAMS OF INFORMATION FROM MULTIPLE SCALES NEED TO BE ACQUIRED AND ACTED ON AT MULTIPLE SCALES.  IN FACT, THE SUPERMOLECULE, THE BIOLOGICAL CELL, THE ASTRONAUTS BODY AND THE SPACESHIP, THOUGH VARYING WIDELY IN SIZES, ARE ALL COMPLEX SYSTEMS PERFORMING COHERENT FUNCTIONS THROUGH HIGHLY DISTRIBUTED MECHANISMS OF SENSING.  INFORMATION PROCESSING AND ACTUATION.  TRANSCENDING ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE DIFFERENCES IN LENGTH SCALES, UCLA VIEWS THE SUPERMOLECULE, THE BIOLOGICAL CELL, THE ASTRONAUTS BODY AND THE SPACE VEHICLE AS CELLS, OBSERVATION POINTS WHERE COHERENCE OF INFORMATION EMERGES FROM COMPLEXITY.  THESE CELLS ARE SYSTEMS THAT MIMIC THE MODES OF INFORMATION PROCESSING NORMALLY ATTRIBUTED TO BIOLOGICAL CELLS.  THE APPLICATION OF NATURES STRATEGY OF DISTRIBUTED MULTILEVEL INFORMATION COLLECTION AND MANAGEMENT IS THE THREAD THAT WILL ACHIEVE A SEAMLESS LINK BETWEEN THE MOLECULAR SCALE NANOTECHNOLOGY OF SENSORS, ACTUATORS AND COMPUTATION, THE ASTRONAUTS AND THE SPACE VEHICLE.  BY MIMICKING THE COMPLEXITY OF MULTISCALE INFORMATION MANAGEMENT OF LIVING SYSTEMS COUPLED WITH THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW NANO TECHNOLOGIES, SPACE EXPLORATION WILL ENTER A NEW ERA.  WITH THIS OUT-OF-BOX CONCEPT, UCLA PROPOSED THE INSTITUTE FOR CELL MIMETIC SPACE EXPLORATION (CMISE).  THIS INSTITUTE WILL BE DEVOTED TO THE - DEVELOPMENT OF CELL MIMETIC SYSTEMS, CONSISTING OF SENSORS, ACTUATORS AND ENERGY SOURCES.  DEVELOPMENT OF MULTI-SCALE INFORMATION PROCESSING TECHNIQUES, I.E., INFORMATICS.  DEVELOPMENT OF SCALABLE TECHNOLOGIES FOR SPACE BIOLOGICAL EXPERIMENTS, ASTRONAUT HEALTH MONITORING AND SPACESHIP RESOURCE MANAGEMENT.  DEVELOPMENT OF AN INTERDISCIPLINARY EDUCATION PROGRAM FOR EDUCATING FUTURE GENERATIONS OF YOUNG SPACE ENGINEERS AND SCIENTISTS.  CMISE ENVISIONS THAT ITS STRATEGY OF USING THE BIOLOGICAL MODEL OF HIERARCHICAL CELLULAR ORGANIZATION FOR THE APPLICATION OF NANOTECHNOLOGY AND THE MANAGEMENT OF INFORMATION WILL BE THE MODEL OF SPACE SYSTEM DESIGN THAT WILL DEFINE THE TECHNOLOGY FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS OF SPACE EXPLORERS.  THE GOAL OF THE CMISE EDUCATION PROGRAM IS TO TRAIN A CONTINUOUS STREAM OF YOUNG SPACE EXPLORERS.  THE PROGRAM WILL ENCOMPASS THE ENTIRE EDUCATIONAL SPECTRUM:  THE DEVELOPMENT OF LEARNING TOOLS FOR K-12, RESEARCH EXPERIENCES FOR UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS AND SUPPORT FOR PH.D. GRADUATE TRAINING.  SPECIAL ATTENTION WILL BE PAID TO THE RECRUITMENT OF UNDER-REPRESENTED STUDENTS.  STUDENTS OF THE CMISE PROGRAM WILL BE TRAINED IN A NEW GENERATION OF CROSS-DISCIPLINARY TECHNOLOGIES THAT ARE ABSOLUTELY NECESSARY TO SUPPORT THE NEXT GENERATION OF SPACE EXPLORERS.

THE ETS CONTRACT WAS INITIALLY ESTABLISHED IN 1985, AND HAS EXISTED CONTINUOUSLY SINCE THEN, WITH A FEW CHANGES IN SCOPE, STRUCTURE, AND SIZE.  TASK ORDERS (TOS) CONSTITUTE THE MECHANISM FOR ORDERING SERVICES ON THIS CONTRACT. .  THE TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS IN THE TOS (CALLED FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS) APPLY TO SPECIFIC WBS ELEMENTS OF THE CONTRACT, WITH THE NUMBERING FOR EACH SECTION CORRESPONDING TO THE APPLICABLE WBS NOMENCLATURE.  THE WORK ON TOS GENERALLY REPRESENTS ONGOING EFFORTS, RATHER THAN NEWLY DEFINED OR CLOSED-ENDED WORK.  THERE IS AN ALLOWANCE FOR WORK TO BE ORDERED OF A CLOSED-ENDED NATURE UNDER A SPECIAL PROJECTS AND STUDIES WBS.  THE WBS ELEMENTS IN THE STATEMENT OF SOW ARE DIVIDED FOUR SECTIONS:SECTION 1, RESEARCH ENGINEERING SUPPORT: THIS SECTION DESCRIBES REQUIREMENTS FOR SUPPORT OF RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES AT DRYDEN DIRECTLY UNDER THE PURVIEW OF THE RESEARCH ENGINEERING DIRECTORATE. SECTION 2, MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS SUPPORT: THIS SECTION DESCRIBES REQUIREMENTS FOR SUPPORT OF FUNCTIONS WITHIN THE SCOPE OF THE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM SUPPORT OFFICE (MSSO) TO MAINTAIN, ASSESS, AND IMPROVE THE DRYDEN MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (DMS). SECTION 3, CHIEF ENGINEERS OFFICE SUPPORT: THIS SECTION DESCRIBES REQUIREMENTS FOR SUPPORT OF THE DFRC CHIEF ENGINEERS OFFICE AND INCLUDES SPECIAL PROJECTS AND STUDIES IN THE AREAS OF TOTAL RISK MANAGEMENT AND INDEPENDENT ASSESSMENT AND REVIEW. SECTION 4, PUBLIC AFFAIRS, COMMERCIALIZATION, EDUCATION OUTREACH, AND HISTORY OFFICE SUPPORT: THIS SECTION DESCRIBES REQUIREMENTS FOR SUPPORT OF  THE DRYDEN PUBLIC AFFAIRS OFFICE, AND INCLUDES BOTH ONGOING WORK AND SPECIAL PROJECTS AND STUDIES IN THE AREAS OF PUBLIC AFFAIRS, COMMUNICATE KNOWLEDGE, EDUCATION AND OUTREACH PROGRAMS, COMMERCIALIZATION AND TECHNOLOGY UTILIZATION, AND NASA HISTORY.

VARIOUS ANALYTICAL MODELS AND TEST MODELS ARE REQUIRED. THE EFFORT INCLUDES GROUND SUPPORT EQUIPMENT AND TEST AND CALIBRATION EQUIPMENT.  IT ALSO INCLUDES A DESIGN CONCEPT REVIEW INSTRUMENT DELIVERY, STORAGE, POST-DELIVERY BENCH TESTING, SPACECRAFT INTEGRATION SUPPORT, PRE-LAUNCH AND POST-LAUNCH SUPPORT.  REPORTING, REVIEWS AND DOCUMENTATION OF ALL ASPECTS OF THE PROGRAM ARE REQUIRED. THE DELIVERABLE EARTH OBSERVING SYSTEM (EOS) AMSU-A INSTRUMENT IS A PFM AND OPTIONAL FLIGHT MODEL (FM).AMSU-A IS PLANNED FOR FLIGHT ON THE EOS PM SPACECRAFT.  AMSU-A SHALL BE COMPATIBLE WITH THE EOS PM SPACECRAFT INTERFACES, AND   SHALL MEET THE IN-ORBIT LIFETIME REQUIREMENT OF 3 YEARS WITH A GOAL OF 5 YEARS WITHOUT IN-ORBIT SERVICING.THE PROGRAM PHASE LEADING TO DELIVERY OF THE PFM SHALL BE REFERRED TO AS THE "BASIC PHASE" AND SHALL BE SUBDIVIDED INTO TWO SUB-PHASES, THE "SUPPORT PHASE" AND THE "IMPLEMENTATION PHASE." THE SUPPORT PHASE SHALL PROVIDE TECHNICAL AND PROGRAM MANAGEMENT SUPPORT TO ADDRESS: (1) THE EVOLVING SPACECRAFT INTERFACES, (2) SPECIAL INSTRUMENT STUDIES AND (3) PROGRAM PLANNING FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION PHASE. PHASE 1 SHALL BE AN ASSESSMENT TO DETERMINE WHAT AREAS OF THE METSAT INSTRUMENT REQUIRE REDESIGN. OBSOLETE COMPONENTS ARE TO BE REPLACED BY NEW COMPONENTS ONLY AFTER DESIGN ANALYSIS HAS BEEN PERFORMED AND MARGINS ARE ANALYTICALLY DEMONSTRATED. IMPROVEMENTS THAT HAVE HERITAGE IN THE EOS AMSU-A INSTRUMENT SHALL BE CONSIDERED AND PRESENTED TO THE GOVERNMENT FOR APPROVAL. PHASE 2 SHALL MAKE AN ASSESSMENT OF ALL DRAWINGS, PROCUREMENTS SPECIFICATIONS, MANUFACTURING FLOWS, SHOP ORDERS, TEST FIXTURES, TEST EQUIPMENT AND TEST PROCEDURES IN ORDER TO IDENTIFY AREAS THAT ARE DEFICIENT AND/OR REQUIRE UPGRADES.  PHASE 3 WILL ACCOMPLISH THOSE ITEMS IDENTIFIED AS A RESULT OF PHASES 1 AND 2.  PHASE 4 IS THE IMPLEMENTATION PHASE WHICH INCLUDES THE FABRICATION, TEST AND CALIBRATION OF THE METSAT INSTRUMENTS.

VARIOUS ANALYTICAL MODELS AND TEST MODELS ARE REQUIRED. THE EFFORT INCLUDES GROUND SUPPORT EQUIPMENT AND TEST AND CALIBRATION EQUIPMENT.  IT ALSO INCLUDES A DESIGN CONCEPT REVIEW INSTRUMENT DELIVERY, STORAGE, POST-DELIVERY BENCH TESTING, SPACECRAFT INTEGRATION SUPPORT, PRE-LAUNCH AND POST-LAUNCH SUPPORT.  REPORTING, REVIEWS AND DOCUMENTATION OF ALL ASPECTS OF THE PROGRAM ARE REQUIRED. THE DELIVERABLE EARTH OBSERVING SYSTEM (EOS) AMSU-A INSTRUMENT IS A PFM AND OPTIONAL FLIGHT MODEL (FM).AMSU-A IS PLANNED FOR FLIGHT ON THE EOS PM SPACECRAFT.  AMSU-A SHALL BE COMPATIBLE WITH THE EOS PM SPACECRAFT INTERFACES, AND   SHALL MEET THE IN-ORBIT LIFETIME REQUIREMENT OF 3 YEARS WITH A GOAL OF 5 YEARS WITHOUT IN-ORBIT SERVICING.THE PROGRAM PHASE LEADING TO DELIVERY OF THE PFM SHALL BE REFERRED TO AS THE "BASIC PHASE" AND SHALL BE SUBDIVIDED INTO TWO SUB-PHASES, THE "SUPPORT PHASE" AND THE "IMPLEMENTATION PHASE." THE SUPPORT PHASE SHALL PROVIDE TECHNICAL AND PROGRAM MANAGEMENT SUPPORT TO ADDRESS: (1) THE EVOLVING SPACECRAFT INTERFACES, (2) SPECIAL INSTRUMENT STUDIES AND (3) PROGRAM PLANNING FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION PHASE. PHASE 1 SHALL BE AN ASSESSMENT TO DETERMINE WHAT AREAS OF THE METSAT INSTRUMENT REQUIRE REDESIGN. OBSOLETE COMPONENTS ARE TO BE REPLACED BY NEW COMPONENTS ONLY AFTER DESIGN ANALYSIS HAS BEEN PERFORMED AND MARGINS ARE ANALYTICALLY DEMONSTRATED. IMPROVEMENTS THAT HAVE HERITAGE IN THE EOS AMSU-A INSTRUMENT SHALL BE CONSIDERED AND PRESENTED TO THE GOVERNMENT FOR APPROVAL. PHASE 2 SHALL MAKE AN ASSESSMENT OF ALL DRAWINGS, PROCUREMENTS SPECIFICATIONS, MANUFACTURING FLOWS, SHOP ORDERS, TEST FIXTURES, TEST EQUIPMENT AND TEST PROCEDURES IN ORDER TO IDENTIFY AREAS THAT ARE DEFICIENT AND/OR REQUIRE UPGRADES.  PHASE 3 WILL ACCOMPLISH THOSE ITEMS IDENTIFIED AS A RESULT OF PHASES 1 AND 2.  PHASE 4 IS THE IMPLEMENTATION PHASE WHICH INCLUDES THE FABRICATION, TEST AND CALIBRATION OF THE METSAT INSTRUMENTS.

CONTRACTOR IS BOEING ELECTRON DYNAMIC DEVICES._CONTRACT NAS3-02158.  THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROCUREMENT IS TO ADVANCE THE SYSTEMS TECHNOLOGY OF ELECTROSTATIC (ION) PROPULSION POWER PROCESSING BEYOND THE STATE-OF-THE-ART NSTAR TECHNOLOGY.  TECHNOLOGY EFFORTS IN THIS PROGRAM ARE INTENDED TO ENABLE THE DESIGN OF HIGH-PERFORMANCE, HIGH-POWER, ION PROPULSION SYSTEMS. AWARD OF THE OPTION IS DEPENDENT ON A NASA HEADQUARTERS CUSTOMER DECISION TO CONTINUE DEVELOPMENT OF THIS CONCEPT.  THE STATEMENT OF WORK INCLUDES BOTH PHASES OF THE PROJECT.  PHASE 2 IS ASSUMED TO BEGIN IMMEDIATELY UPON COMPLETION OF PHASE I. This effort encompasses the tasks necessary to validate, maintain and improve the science data retrieval algorithms for the HIRDLS products mentioned above. These tasks will continue the ongoing reprocessing, evaluation and validation of the standard HIRDLS products using the current Version 4 and subsequent versions of the algorithm. This effort encompasses the tasks necessary to validate, maintain and improve the science data retrieval algorithms for the HIRDLS products mentioned above. Description: THIS EFFORT IS THE EXTENSION OF THE DEFINITION PHASE (PHASE B) FOR THE EARTH OBSERVING SYSTEM (EOS) SOLAR STELLAR IRRADIANCE COMPARISON EXPERIMENT  (SOLSTICE).  THE OUTPUT OF THE PHASE B EXTENSION WILL BE A CONCEPTUAL DESIGN COST REVIEW (CDCR).  THE STATEMENT OF WORK IS BROKEN DOWN INTO THREE SECTIONS: INSTRUMENT, SCIENCE, AND SCIENCE COMPUTING FACILITY.  THIS IS A PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR (PI) EXPERIMENT TO MAKE LONG-TERM SOLAR OBSERVATIONS WITH THE EOS SOLSTICE INSTRUMENT.  THE MEASUREMENTS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO AN IMPROVED UNDERSTANDING OF THE VARIABLE ENERGY INPUT TO THE EARTH'S ATMOSPHERE WITH SPECIAL EMPHASIS ON THE SUN'S INFLUENCE ON THE TEMPERATURE, STRUCTURE, DYNAMICS AND CHEMISTRY OF THE ATMOSPHERIC SYSTEM.  A FUNDAMENTAL AND SPECIFIC USE OF EOS, REPRESENTING A SUBSTANTIAL CHANGE FROM PAST PRACTICE, IS THE PRODUCTION AND ARCHIVING OF DATA SETS FOR GENERAL SCIENTIFIC USE.  THESE DATA SETS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE CONSTRUCTION OF INTERDISCIPLINARY SCIENCE PRODUCTS.   THIS EFFORT WILL INCLUDE MANAGEMENT OF THE COMPLETE PROGRAM AND ITS COORDINATION.IN PHASE C/D/E, THE UNIVERSITY OF COLORADO (UC) SHALL PROVIDE THE FACILITIES, MATERIALS, SERVICES, AND PERSONNEL NECESSARY TO CONTINUE THE SORCE MISSION. UC SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR MISSION OPERATIONS AND SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE SAFETY OF THE INSTRUMENTS AND THE SPACECRAFT BUS THROUGH A SUBCONTRACT ARRANGEMENT WITH THE SPACECRAFT PROVIDER (ORBITAL SCIENCES CORPORATION). UC SHALL DEVELOP/MAINTAIN ALGORITHMS FOR PRODUCING THE SCIENCE DATA PRODUCTS AS PROPOSED AND APPROVED BY NASA HQ. AFTER THE SCIENCE PRODUCTS HAVE BEEN VALIDATED, THESE PRODUCTS WILL BE TRANSFERRED TO THE GSFC DATA ACHIEVE FOR ACHIEVE AND DISTRIBUTION. THE GROUND SYSTEM USED IN THE SORCE MISSION SHALL MEET ALL NASA SECURITY REQUIREMENTS.

Description: The High Resolution Dynamics Limb Sounce (HIRDLS) is an infrared limb-scanning radiometer designed to sound the upper troposphere, stratosphere, and mesosphere to determine: temperature, the concentrations of O3, H2O, CH4, N2O, HNO3, N2O5, CFC11, CFC12,  CIONO12  , and aerosols; and the locations of polar stratospheric clouds and cloud tops. This effort encompasses the tasks necessary to validate, maintain and improve the science data retrieval algorithms for the HIRDLS products mentioned above. Description: STTR 2005, PHASE II PROJECT ENTITLED AERODYNAMIC EFFICIENCY ENHANCEMENTS FOR AIR VEHICLES. A system for autonomous detection and exploitation of weather phenomena for endurance or range enhancement for loitering unmanned air vehicles. The system is to consist of hardware and software for coarse identification of geographical areas where advantageous weather phenomena (such as soaring conditions) are present. Custom autopilot and sensors will enable the fine detection of the phenomena and cause the UAV to adopt an optimal flight path that exploits the phenomena. The system will consist of custom hardware, software, and sensors. A simulation of the system was demonstrated in Phase I, which is to be rendered in hardware in Phase II, including complete full flight test of the system on a 40 pound class UAV. The anticipated result being high endurance schemes for loitering UAVs, innovative flight control systems for UAVs, optimal flight path determination and execution. These developments dovetail with current NASA efforts to develop more intelligent and autonomous air vehicles for use in science mission, military and homeland security missions. The concepts and systems can be ported to small manned aircraft as well. The system as proposed can be used to increase the endurance or range, and/or reduce the fuel consumption of loitering air vehicles operating at low to medium altitudes. There are no UAVs currently having thermal soaring capability. By endowing UAVs with soaring capability, endurance can be enhanced and a framework will exist for next generation UAVs that can sense beneficial atmospheric conditions, couple it with data from online sources, and adapt to exploit the prevailing conditions optimally to achieve increased endurance range. These methods can be adopted for extending the endurance of small aircraft in emergency situations as well. The autopilot could be used by sport glider and motorglider pilots. Military, Homeland Security and science missions are increasing their uses of unmanned air vehicles. Use of this technology will also be investigated for small (<40 lb) and medium sized (~ 600 lb) UAVs which are being developed for homeland security and science missions.

THE TL SHALL DIRECT AND CONDUCT THE GLAS SCIENCE INVESTIGATION.  THIS WORK INCLUDES, BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO, THE DEVELOPMENT AND  MAINTENANCE OF SOFTWARE TO PRODUCE STANDARD AND SPECIAL DATA PRODUCTS FROM THE OBSERVATIONS MADE BY THE GLAS INSTRUMENT, LEADING THE SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH TO SUPPORT THE EOS SCIENCE PLAN, AND PROVIDING SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT, OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF THE MISSION. THE TL SHALL DIRECT AND COORDINATE THE TM ALGORITHM DEVELOPMENT, AND SHALL PREPARE AND COORDINATE THE TEAM'S SCHEDULES AND BUDGETS WITH THE GLAS CONTRACTING OFFICER'S TECHNICAL REPRESENTATIVE (COTR). IN CONSONANCE WITH THE ABOVE ACTIVITIES, THE TL/TM SHALL CARRY OUT SCIENTIFIC INVESTIGATIONS WITH DATA FROM THE INSTRUMENT LEADING TO THE PUBLICATION OF RESULTS IN PROCEEDINGS OF SCIENTIFIC MEETINGS AND IN REFEREED SCIENTIFIC JOURNALS. THE GLAS STANDARD DATA PRODUCTS WILL BE GENERATED ROUTINELY AT THE NATIONAL SNOW AND ICE DATA CENTER'S (NSIDC)DISTRIBUTED ACTIVE ARCHIVE CENTER (DAAC) AT THE UNIVERSITY OF COLORADO OR AT A LOCATION SPECIFIED BY THE COTR.

Description: Statement of Work: Jean-Claude Roger's work will be related to the improvement of the aerosol optical properties with respect to modeling their radiative forcing effects and their use in atmospheric correction. The work will focus on enhancing the AERONET retrieval, in particular developing, testing and validating a consistent radiative transfer package that will be used in the forward mode for the inversion, for general usage by the user community and for the computation of the radiative forcing. This package will be based on the 6S radiative transfer vectorial code. The remote sensing data used for validation and testing will be principally from the MODIS (Terra and Aqua instrument), but MISR data will also be used in the refinement phase of the projects. Validation data from the EOS project will be used to validate shortwave irradiance measurements. Concurrently with the establishment of a statistically robust error budget, the synergy between the chemical and optical characterization of aerosol will be investigated with respect to their radiative effect and environmental impacts.

Description: Justification for sole source procurement: We recommend this purchase be sole source from Sigma Space Corporation. Description: NEW RESEARCH GRANT AWARD FUNDING WITH CONGRESSIONAL EARMARK FUNDS ENTITLED "EARLY REGULATORY ELEMENTS OF THE GRAVITY-SPECIFIC TRANSCRIPTIONAL NETWORK"SINGLE YEAR AWARD FULLY FUNDED WITH 2004 FISCAL YEAR FUNDING.PROPOSAL ABSTRACT:  THE RESPONSE OF THE PLANTS TO GRAVITY INVOLVES A SENSING MECHANISM, INITIATING A SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION PATHWAY, WHICH RESULTS IN CHANGES IN GENE EXPRESSION.  THE ONLY LINK BETWEEN GRAVITY RESPONSE AND TRASCRIPTIONAL CHANGES KNOWN SO FAR IS MEDIATED BY AUXIN.  USING WHOLE GENOME MICRO-ARRAY TECHNOLOGY, WE HAVE IDENTIFIED GENES THAT RESPOND EXCLUSIVELY TO GRAVITY STIMULATION BY NOT TO MECHANICAL STIMULATION IN THE ARABIDOPSIS THALIANA ROOT APEX.  THE FASTEST TRASCIPTIONAL GRAVITY - SPECIFIC RESPONSES OCCUR WITHIN LESS THAN ONE MINUTES AFTER GRAVITY STIMULATION.  AT THESE EARLY TIME POINTS, MOST GENES INCOLVED IN HOMRONE-MEDICATED RESPONSES (AUXIN, ETHYLENE) DID NOT SHOW SPECIFITIY TO GRAVITY STIMULATION.  THE MAJORITY OF EARLY GRAVITY-SPECIFIC GENES WERE NOT INDUCED AFTER GRAVITY STIMULATION OF TRANSGENIC ARABIDOPSIS PLANTS WWE HAVE DEVELOPED WHICH EXHIBITITH A DELAYED AND SLOW RESPONSE TO GRAVITY.  THESE TRANSGENIC PLANTS HAVE REDUCED LEVELS OF INOSITOL - 1, 4, 5-TRISPOSPHATE (INSP3), A VERY EARLY COMPONENT OF GRAVITROPIC SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION.

Description: RADIOISOTOPE POWER CONVERSION TECHNOLOGY.  THIS PROGRAM ADDRESSES THE REQUEST FOR RPS CONVERSION TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT IN NRA-02-OSS-01.  THE GOAL OF THE PROJECT IS TO DEMONSTRATE A STATIC TPV POWER CONVERTER SUITABLE FOR USE WITH AN ADVANCED RPS USING GPHS HEAT SOURCES, BRINGING THIS CONVERTER TECHNOLOGY (RTPV) TO TRL 5 AT THE END OF THE THIRD YEAR.  TPV CONVERTS RADIANT ENERGY FROM A HOT EMITTER TO ELECTRICAL POWER USING PV CELLS.  TPV USES ADVANCED PV CELLS TO UTILIZE A BROADER, SPECTRALLY-TUNED RANGE OF WAVELENGTHS FOR MORE EFFICIENT POWER CONVERSION THAN SOLAR PV CELLS.  SPECTRAL CONTROL, INCLUDING SELECTIVE EMITTER, PV CELL, AND FILTER CHARACTERISTICS, IS KEY TO HIGH PERFORMANCE.  LIFETIME TESTS ARE PLANNED.  STEPS IN THE DEVELOPMENT INCLUDE: YEAR 1:  DEVELOP THE TPV MODULE (TRL 3) - DEVELOP, FABRICATE, DEMONSTRATE AND SELECT THE BEST OPTIONS FROM VARIOUS EMITTERS, PV CELLS, AND FILTER APPROACHES, WITH SUPPORT EFFORTS TO DEVELOP THE PRELIMINARY CONVERTER DESIGN AND TO ADDRESS TWO KEY TECHNICAL QUESTIONS ABOUT CONVERTER LIFETIME:  RADIATION EFFECTS ON THE PV CELLS AND MATERIALS TRANSFER.  YEAR 2:  DEMONSTRATE A PROTOTYPIC RTPV OPTICAL CAVITY/CONVERTER (TRL 4) - FABRICATE AND TEST AN ELECTRICALLY HEATED BASELINE CONVERTER WITH PROTOTYPICAL DESIGN (OPTICAL CAVITY/CONVERTER AND IMMEDIATE STRUCTURE), WITH SUPPORTING MODELING AND TESTING EFFORTS, AS WELL AS CONTINUE RADIATION EXPOSURE AND MATERIALS LIFE TESTS.  YEAR 3:  DEMONSTRATE A BREADBOARD RTPV OPTICAL CAVITY/CONVERTER AND LONG-TERM PERFORMANCE OF A PROTOTYPIC CONVERTER (TRL 5) - BUILD A BREADBOARD MODEL WITH THE OPTIMUM CONVERTER DESIGN AND A POWER CONVERTER MODULE, THEN TEST IN A THERMAL VACUUM CHAMBER; CONCLUDE SUPPORTING EFFORTS TO DEMONSTRATE LONG LIFE WITH MINIMAL POWER DECREASE.  RECENT ADVANCES IN INGAAS PV CELL, FILTER, AND SLECTIVE EMITTER TECHNOLOGY HAVE SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVED THE PERFORMANCE OF TPV SYSTEMS TO THE POINT THAT TPV SYSTEMS ARE NOW COMPETITIVE IN CONVERSION EFFICIENCY A ND SPECIFIC POWER WITH DYNAMIC POWER SYSTEMS.  SPECIFICALLY, TPV CONVERTER EFFIFIENCY OF 20% HAS BEEN DEMONSTRATED AT 1330 K FOR SINGLE CELLS (SIERGIEJ ET AL. 2002) AND FOR A 16-CELL ARRAY IN AN OPTICAL CAVITY DURING THE YEAR 1 EFFORT.  WE EXPECT TO IMPROVE ON THIS.

Description: RADIOISOTOPE POWER CONVERSION TECHNOLOGY.  THIS PROGRAM ADDRESSES THE REQUEST FOR RPS CONVERSION TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT IN NRA-02-OSS-01.  THE GOAL OF THE PROJECT IS TO DEMONSTRATE A STATIC TPV POWER CONVERTER SUITABLE FOR USE WITH AN ADVANCED RPS USING GPHS HEAT SOURCES, BRINGING THIS CONVERTER TECHNOLOGY (RTPV) TO TRL 5 AT THE END OF THE THIRD YEAR.  TPV CONVERTS RADIANT ENERGY FROM A HOT EMITTER TO ELECTRICAL POWER USING PV CELLS.  TPV USES ADVANCED PV CELLS TO UTILIZE A BROADER, SPECTRALLY-TUNED RANGE OF WAVELENGTHS FOR MORE EFFICIENT POWER CONVERSION THAN SOLAR PV CELLS.  SPECTRAL CONTROL, INCLUDING SELECTIVE EMITTER, PV CELL, AND FILTER CHARACTERISTICS, IS KEY TO HIGH PERFORMANCE.  LIFETIME TESTS ARE PLANNED.  STEPS IN THE DEVELOPMENT INCLUDE: YEAR 1:  DEVELOP THE TPV MODULE (TRL 3) - DEVELOP, FABRICATE, DEMONSTRATE AND SELECT THE BEST OPTIONS FROM VARIOUS EMITTERS, PV CELLS, AND FILTER APPROACHES, WITH SUPPORT EFFORTS TO DEVELOP THE PRELIMINARY CONVERTER DESIGN AND TO ADDRESS TWO KEY TECHNICAL QUESTIONS ABOUT CONVERTER LIFETIME:  RADIATION EFFECTS ON THE PV CELLS AND MATERIALS TRANSFER.  YEAR 2:  DEMONSTRATE A PROTOTYPIC RTPV OPTICAL CAVITY/CONVERTER (TRL 4) - FABRICATE AND TEST AN ELECTRICALLY HEATED BASELINE CONVERTER WITH PROTOTYPICAL DESIGN (OPTICAL CAVITY/CONVERTER AND IMMEDIATE STRUCTURE), WITH SUPPORTING MODELING AND TESTING EFFORTS, AS WELL AS CONTINUE RADIATION EXPOSURE AND MATERIALS LIFE TESTS.  YEAR 3:  DEMONSTRATE A BREADBOARD RTPV OPTICAL CAVITY/CONVERTER AND LONG-TERM PERFORMANCE OF A PROTOTYPIC CONVERTER (TRL 5) - BUILD A BREADBOARD MODEL WITH THE OPTIMUM CONVERTER DESIGN AND A POWER CONVERTER MODULE, THEN TEST IN A THERMAL VACUUM CHAMBER; CONCLUDE SUPPORTING EFFORTS TO DEMONSTRATE LONG LIFE WITH MINIMAL POWER DECREASE.  RECENT ADVANCES IN INGAAS PV CELL, FILTER, AND SLECTIVE EMITTER TECHNOLOGY HAVE SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVED THE PERFORMANCE OF TPV SYSTEMS TO THE POINT THAT TPV SYSTEMS ARE NOW COMPETITIVE IN CONVERSION EFFICIENCY A ND SPECIFIC POWER WITH DYNAMIC POWER SYSTEMS.  SPECIFICALLY, TPV CONVERTER EFFIFIENCY OF 20% HAS BEEN DEMONSTRATED AT 1330 K FOR SINGLE CELLS (SIERGIEJ ET AL. 2002) AND FOR A 16-CELL ARRAY IN AN OPTICAL CAVITY DURING THE YEAR 1 EFFORT.  WE EXPECT TO IMPROVE ON THIS.
